tools.description: Sets or updates a team's permission level for a repository within an organization; the team must be a member of the organization.

tools.name: Add project collaborator
tools.description: Adds a specified GitHub user as a collaborator to an existing organization project with a given permission level. Note: This endpoint is for organization projects (classic). You must be an organization owner or a project admin to add a collaborator. Classic projects are being deprecated in favor of the new Projects experience.

tools.name: Add a repository to an app installation
tools.description: Adds a repository to a GitHub App installation, granting the app access; requires authenticated user to have admin rights for the repository and access to the installation.

tools.name: Add repo to org secret with selected access
tools.description: Adds a repository to an existing organization-level GitHub Actions secret that is configured for 'selected' repository access.

tools.name: Add selected repo to org secret
tools.description: Grants an existing repository access to an existing organization-level Dependabot secret when the secret's visibility is set to 'selected'; the repository must belong to the organization, and the call succeeds without change if access already exists.

tools.name: Add runner labels
tools.description: Adds and appends custom labels to a self-hosted repository runner, which must be registered and active.

tools.name: Add selected repository to an organization secret
tools.description: Adds a repository to an organization secret's access list when the secret's visibility is 'selected'; this operation is idempotent.

tools.name: Add selected repository to an organization variable
tools.description: Grants a repository access to an organization-level GitHub Actions variable, if that variable's visibility is set to 'selected_repositories'.

tools.name: Add a selected repository to a user secret
tools.description: Grants a specified repository access to an authenticated user's existing Codespaces secret, enabling Codespaces created for that repository to use the secret.

tools.name: Add social accounts for the authenticated user
tools.description: Adds one or more social media links (which must be valid, full URLs for platforms supported by GitHub) to the authenticated user's public GitHub profile.

tools.name: Add status check contexts
tools.description: Adds status check contexts to a protected branch's required status checks. This action appends new status check contexts to the existing list of required status checks for a protected branch. The branch must already have branch protection enabled with status checks configured. Note: The 'contexts' parameter is deprecated by GitHub in favor of 'checks' array. For new implementations, consider using update_status_check_protection with the 'checks' parameter instead.

tools.name: Add sub-issue to an issue
tools.description: Tool to add a sub-issue to a parent GitHub issue using GraphQL. Use when you need to establish a parent-child relationship between issues. Requires the 'sub_issues' GraphQL feature to be enabled.

tools.name: Add team access restrictions
tools.description: Adds teams to the list of teams with push access to a protected branch. This action grants additional teams push access to a protected branch. Unlike 'Set team access restrictions' (PUT), this action adds to the existing list rather than replacing it entirely. Prerequisites: - The repository must be owned by an organization (not a personal account) - The branch must have protection rules enabled - The branch protection must have restrictions configured - The teams must exist in the organization and have repository access

tools.name: Add user access restrictions
tools.description: Adds users to the list of people allowed to push to a protected branch in an organization repository. Important notes: - This action only works on organization-owned repositories (not personal repos) - The branch must already have protection rules with restrictions enabled - Users must have write access to the repository to be added - The combined total of users, apps, and teams is limited to 100 items

tools.name: Add users to codespaces access for an organization
tools.description: Adds organization members to the list of users granted Codespaces access billed to the organization. IMPORTANT: This endpoint requires the organization's Codespaces billing access to be set to 'selected_members' mode. If not already configured, use the GITHUB_MANAGE_ACCESS_CONTROL_FOR_ORGANIZATION_CODESPACES action first to set visibility to 'selected_members'.

tools.name: Get GitHub API root
tools.description: Retrieves a map of all top-level GitHub REST API resource URLs and their templates.

tools.name: Approve a workflow run for a fork pull request
tools.description: Approves a workflow run from a forked repository's pull request; call this when such a run requires manual approval due to workflow configuration.

tools.name: Assign an organization role to a team
tools.description: Assigns an existing organization-level role (identified by `role_id`) to a team (identified by `team_slug`) within a GitHub organization (`org`), provided the organization, team, and role already exist.

tools.name: Assign an organization role to a user
tools.description: Assigns a specific organization role to a user who is a member or an outside collaborator in a GitHub organization, using a valid role ID.

tools.name: List Docker Migration Conflicting Packages
tools.description: List Docker packages with migration conflicts for the authenticated user. This endpoint lists all Docker packages owned by the authenticated user that encountered namespace conflicts during the Docker-to-GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) migration. Conflicts occur when a package with the same name exists in both the legacy Docker registry and GHCR. IMPORTANT: The Docker registry for GitHub Packages was deprecated on Feb 24, 2025. This endpoint may return a 400 error with message 'Package migration for docker is no longer supported' as the migration period has ended. In this case, the action returns an informative response instead of failing. Use case: Identifying packages that require manual migration to GHCR. Required scope: read:packages (for OAuth and personal access tokens).

tools.name: Block a user
tools.description: Blocks an existing individual GitHub user (not an organization or your own account), preventing them from interacting with your account and repositories.

tools.name: Block a user from an organization
tools.description: Blocks a GitHub user from an organization, preventing their contributions, collaboration, and forking of the organization's repositories. Requires admin or 'Blocking users' organization permission (write access).

tools.name: Cancel a GitHub Pages deployment
tools.description: Cancels an existing, ongoing or queued GitHub Pages deployment for a repository using its `pages_deployment_id`.

tools.name: Cancel sponsorship
tools.description: Tool to cancel an active GitHub sponsorship using GraphQL. Use when you need to terminate a sponsorship relationship between a sponsor and a sponsorable entity. Either sponsor ID/login and sponsorable ID/login must be provided.

tools.name: Cancel a workflow run
tools.description: Cancels a workflow run in a GitHub repository if it is in a cancellable state (e.g., 'in_progress' or 'queued'). Returns 202 Accepted on success.

tools.name: Check if a gist is starred
tools.description: Checks if a gist is starred by the authenticated user. Returns `is_starred: true` if the gist is starred (HTTP 204), or `is_starred: false` if not starred (HTTP 404). Use this to verify star status before starring/unstarring a gist.

tools.name: Check if pull request merged
tools.description: Checks if a specified GitHub pull request has been merged, indicated by a 204 HTTP status (merged) or 404 (not merged/found).

tools.name: Check if a user can be assigned
tools.description: Verifies if a GitHub user can be assigned to issues in a repository; assignability is confirmed by an HTTP 204 (No Content) response, resulting in an empty 'data' field in the response.

tools.name: Check if a user can be assigned to an issue
tools.description: Checks if a specified GitHub user can be assigned to a given issue within a repository.

tools.name: Check if a user follows another user
tools.description: Checks if a GitHub user `username` follows `target_user`; returns a 204 HTTP status if true, 404 if not or if users are invalid.

tools.name: Check if a user is blocked by the authenticated user
tools.description: Checks if the specified GitHub user is blocked by the authenticated user; a 204 No Content response indicates the user is blocked, while a 404 Not Found indicates they are not.

tools.name: Check if a user is blocked by an organization
tools.description: Checks if a GitHub user is blocked by an organization. Returns is_blocked=True if the user is blocked (HTTP 204), or is_blocked=False if not blocked (HTTP 404). Requires 'Blocking users' organization permission (read access).

tools.name: Check if a user is a repository collaborator
tools.description: Checks if a user is a collaborator on a specified GitHub repository, returning a 204 status if they are, or a 404 status if they are not or if the repository/user does not exist.

tools.name: Check if person is followed by authenticated user
tools.description: Checks if the authenticated GitHub user follows a target GitHub user. Returns a structured response with is_following=True when following (HTTP 204), or is_following=False when not following (HTTP 404).

tools.name: Check private vulnerability reporting status
tools.description: Checks if private vulnerability reporting is enabled for the specified repository.

tools.name: Check public organization membership
tools.description: Tool to check if a user is a public member of an organization. Use when you need to verify public organization membership status.

tools.name: Check team permissions for a project
tools.description: Checks if a team has 'read', 'write', or 'admin' permissions for an organization's specific classic project, returning the project's details if access is confirmed.

tools.name: Check team permissions for a repository
tools.description: Checks a team's permissions for a specific repository within an organization, including permissions inherited from parent teams.

tools.name: Check a token
tools.description: Checks if a GitHub App or OAuth access_token is valid for the specified client_id and retrieves its details, typically to verify its active status and grants. NOTE: This endpoint requires Basic Authentication using the OAuth App's client_id as username and client_secret as password. The access_token parameter must be an OAuth token issued by the specified OAuth App.

tools.name: Clear Project V2 Item Field Value
tools.description: Tool to clear the value of a field for an item in a GitHub Project V2. Use when you need to remove or reset a field value (text, number, date, assignees, labels, single-select, iteration, or milestone fields).

tools.name: Clear repository cache by key
tools.description: Deletes GitHub Actions caches from a repository matching a specific `key` and an optional Git `ref`, used to manage storage or clear outdated/corrupted caches; the action succeeds even if no matching caches are found to delete.

tools.name: Clear self-hosted runner org labels
tools.description: Removes all custom labels from a self-hosted runner for an organization; default labels (e.g., 'self-hosted', 'linux', 'x64') will remain.

tools.name: Commit Multiple Files
tools.description: Tool to atomically create, update, or delete multiple files in a GitHub repository as a single commit. Uses Git Data APIs to avoid SHA mismatch conflicts that occur with the Contents API when multiple files are modified in parallel. Use when you need to make multi-file changes reliably. BRANCH CREATION: When committing to a new branch (e.g., 'fix/my-fix' or 'feature/new-feature'), you MUST provide 'base_branch' (typically 'main' or 'master') to create the branch from. If the branch already exists, base_branch is not needed. This action handles race conditions automatically: if the branch is updated by another commit between fetching the HEAD and updating the reference (resulting in a 422 'not a fast forward' error), the action will retry by refetching the HEAD and rebasing changes. Use max_retries to control this behavior.

tools.name: Compare two commits
tools.description: Compares two commit points (commits, branches, tags, or SHAs) within a repository or across forks, using `BASE...HEAD` or `OWNER:REF...OWNER:REF` format for the `basehead` parameter.

tools.name: Configure JIT runner for an org
tools.description: Generates a JIT configuration for a GitHub organization's new self-hosted runner to run a single job then unregister; requires admin:org scope and the runner_group_id must exist in the organization.

tools.name: Configure OIDC subject claim template
tools.description: Sets or updates the OIDC subject claim customization template for an existing GitHub organization by specifying which claims (e.g., 'repo', 'actor') form the OIDC token's subject (`sub`). This action customizes which claim keys are included in the OIDC subject claim for the specified organization. It allows for fine-tuning the content of the subject claim based on organizational needs.

tools.name: Convert an organization member to outside collaborator
tools.description: Converts an existing organization member, who is not an owner, to an outside collaborator, restricting their access to explicitly granted repositories.

tools.name: Create a blob
tools.description: Creates a Git blob in a repository, requiring content and encoding ('utf-8' or 'base64'). Requires write access to the repository.

tools.name: Create a check run
tools.description: Creates a new check run for a specific commit in a repository, used by external services to report status, detailed feedback, annotations, and images directly within the GitHub UI. NOTE: This endpoint requires GitHub App authentication - OAuth tokens and personal access tokens cannot create check runs.

tools.name: Create a check suite
tools.description: Creates a new check suite for a specific commit (`head_sha`) in an original repository (not a fork). IMPORTANT: This endpoint requires a GitHub App installation access token - OAuth tokens and classic personal access tokens cannot use this endpoint. GitHub dispatches a `check_suite` webhook event with the `requested` action upon success.

tools.name: Create a codespace for the authenticated user
tools.description: Creates a GitHub Codespace for the authenticated user, requiring a JSON request body with either `repository_id` (integer) or a `pull_request` object (containing `pull_request_number` (integer) and `repository_id` (integer)). This action allows users to set up a development environment quickly by creating a codespace from a specified repository or pull request.

tools.name: Create a codespace from a pull request
tools.description: Creates a GitHub Codespace for an open pull request in a Codespaces-enabled repository, with options to customize its configuration.

tools.name: Create a codespace in a repository
tools.description: Creates a GitHub Codespace for the authenticated user in a specified repository, which must be accessible and use a valid `devcontainer.json` if `devcontainer_path` is specified.

tools.name: Create a commit
tools.description: Creates a new commit in a GitHub repository; the `tree` SHA and any `parents` SHAs must already exist in the repository.

tools.name: Create a commit comment
tools.description: Creates a comment on a specific commit, or on a specific line if `path` and `position` are provided.

tools.name: Create a commit status
tools.description: Sets a commit's status (e.g., error, failure, pending, success from CI/CD) for a given SHA; max 1000 statuses per SHA/context.

tools.name: Create a custom organization role
tools.description: Creates a custom role with defined permissions within a GitHub organization.

tools.name: Create a deploy key
tools.description: Creates a deploy key for a repository; the repository must exist and be accessible, and the provided key must be a valid public SSH key.

tools.name: Create a deployment
tools.description: Creates a GitHub deployment for an existing repository, targeting a specific ref (branch, tag, or SHA) that must also exist within the repository.

tools.name: Create a deployment branch policy
tools.description: Creates a deployment branch or tag policy for an existing environment in a GitHub repository, using a Ruby File.fnmatch pattern (where `*` doesn't match `/`) to specify which branches or tags are deployable.

tools.name: Create a deployment status
tools.description: Creates a status for an existing deployment, updating its operational state, associated URLs, and description.

tools.name: Create a discussion
tools.description: Creates a new discussion post on a specific team's page within an organization.

tools.name: Create a discussion comment
tools.description: Creates a new comment on an existing team discussion within a GitHub organization.

tools.name: Create a fork
tools.description: Creates a fork of an accessible repository, optionally into a specific organization, with a new name, or copying only the default branch.

tools.name: Create a gist
tools.description: Creates a new gist on GitHub with provided files, an optional description, and public/secret visibility.

tools.name: Create a gist comment
tools.description: Creates a new comment on a specified GitHub gist.

tools.name: Create a GitHub App from a manifest
tools.description: Use this action to complete the GitHub App Manifest flow (step 3 of 3) by exchanging the temporary authorization `code` for the app's full configuration, including credentials and private key. The code is provided via redirect URL after creating the app through GitHub's web interface and must be used within 1 hour.

tools.name: Create a github pages deployment
tools.description: Creates a GitHub Pages deployment for a repository using a specified artifact and OIDC token, provided GitHub Pages is enabled and the artifact (containing static assets) is accessible.

tools.name: Create a github pages site
tools.description: Configures or updates GitHub Pages for a repository, setting build type and source; ensure a Pages workflow exists for 'workflow' `build_type`, or `source_branch` exists for 'legacy' or unspecified `build_type`. This action allows users to effectively manage their GitHub Pages site settings, specifying how the site is built and where the source files are located.

tools.name: Create a label
tools.description: Creates a new label in a specified GitHub repository, provided the repository exists and the user has write permissions.

tools.name: Create a milestone
tools.description: Creates a milestone in a GitHub repository for tracking progress on issues or pull requests; requires repository existence and user write permissions.

tools.name: Create an autolink reference for a repository
tools.description: Creates a repository autolink to automatically convert text references (e.g., 'TICKET-123') into hyperlinks, using a unique `key_prefix` and a `url_template` that includes `<num>`.

tools.name: Create an environment variable
tools.description: Creates an encrypted environment variable for a pre-existing environment within a GitHub repository; will fail if the variable name already exists.

tools.name: Create an issue
tools.description: Creates a new issue in a GitHub repository, requiring the repository to exist and have issues enabled; specific fields like assignees, milestone, or labels may require push access.

tools.name: Create an issue comment
tools.description: Creates a new comment on an existing GitHub issue or pull request within the specified repository.

tools.name: Create an organization project
tools.description: Creates a new classic project board within a specified GitHub organization. Note: This action uses GitHub's Projects (classic) REST API. The classic projects feature may be disabled in some organizations, and GitHub recommends migrating to Projects V2 (accessible via GraphQL API) for new projects. Requirements: - The authenticated user must be an organization member with project creation permissions - Classic projects must be enabled for the organization - Requires 'repo' and 'admin:org' or 'write:org' scopes

tools.name: Create an organization repository
tools.description: Creates a new repository within a specified GitHub organization, with options for detailed configuration including visibility, features, merge strategies, initial commit, and templates.

tools.name: Create an organization variable
tools.description: Creates a new, uniquely named GitHub Actions variable for an organization, with configurable repository access visibility (all, private, or selected).

tools.name: Create an organization webhook
tools.description: Creates a webhook for a GitHub organization to deliver event notifications to a configured URL.

tools.name: Create a project card
tools.description: Creates a project card in a GitHub project column (classic projects only). DEPRECATION NOTICE: GitHub Projects (classic) was sunset on August 23, 2024. This API only works with existing classic project columns. New classic projects cannot be created. Consider using GitHub Projects V2 (GraphQL API) instead. The request body must contain either: - `note`: A text note for the card - OR `content_id` AND `content_type`: To associate an issue or pull request

tools.name: Create a project column (Classic - Deprecated)
tools.description: Creates a new column in a GitHub project (classic). DEPRECATION NOTICE: GitHub Classic Projects (V1) and its REST API were sunset on April 1, 2025. This action will return a 404 error on GitHub.com. For new projects, use GitHub Projects V2 which uses the GraphQL API instead. See: https://github.blog/changelog/2024-05-23-sunset-notice-projects-classic/

tools.name: Create a pull request
tools.description: Creates a pull request in a GitHub repository, requiring existing `base` and `head` branches; `title` or `issue` must be provided.

tools.name: Create a reference
tools.description: Creates a NEW Git reference (branch or tag) in a repository. IMPORTANT: This action ONLY creates NEW references - if the reference already exists, it will fail with a 422 'Reference already exists' error. To update an existing reference, use the 'Update a reference' (GITHUB_UPDATE_A_REFERENCE) action instead. The repository must not be empty prior to this operation.

tools.name: Create a registration token for an organization
tools.description: Generates a temporary (one-hour) registration token to add a new self-hosted runner to an organization for GitHub Actions.

tools.name: Create a registration token for a repository
tools.description: Generates a time-limited token required to register a new self-hosted runner with a specific repository.

tools.name: Create a release
tools.description: Creates a release in a GitHub repository for a specified tag; the tag must be unique for published releases, and if a `discussion_category_name` is given, it must already exist.

tools.name: Create a remove token for an organization
tools.description: Generates a token, valid for one hour, to authenticate removing a self-hosted runner from an organization.

tools.name: Create a remove token for a repository
tools.description: Generates a temporary (one-hour validity) token required to unregister and remove a self-hosted runner from a repository.

tools.name: Create a reply for a review comment
tools.description: Posts a reply to a specific review comment on a GitHub pull request, requiring the repository, pull request, and original comment to exist, and a non-empty reply body.

tools.name: Create a repository dispatch event
tools.description: Triggers a GitHub Actions workflow or a webhook on a repository by creating a repository dispatch event, allowing programmatic triggering of workflows based on events outside of GitHub.

tools.name: Create a repository for the authenticated user
tools.description: Creates a new repository for the authenticated user, optionally within an organization if `team_id` is specified.

tools.name: Create a repository from an unpublished codespace
tools.description: Publishes the specified codespace to a new repository, using the codespace's current state as the initial commit.

tools.name: Create a repository project
tools.description: Creates a new GitHub Projects V2 project board linked to a specified repository. Note: This action uses GitHub's Projects V2 GraphQL API. The legacy Projects V1 REST API has been sunset by GitHub. The project is owned by the repository owner (user or organization) and linked to the specified repository.

tools.name: Create a repository ruleset
tools.description: Creates a uniquely named ruleset for a repository, defining rules for branches or tags with specified enforcement, conditions, and bypass actors.

tools.name: Create a repository using a template
tools.description: Creates a new repository from an existing template repository; the authenticated user must have access to the template and, if creating in an organization, repository creation permissions within it.

tools.name: Create a repository variable
tools.description: Creates a new, unencrypted variable in a repository for GitHub Actions workflows; fails if a variable with the same name already exists.

tools.name: Create a repository webhook
tools.description: Creates a webhook for a specified repository; requires admin permissions on the repository.

tools.name: Create a review comment for a pull request
tools.description: Creates a review comment on a pull request's diff, targeting a specific line, range of lines, an entire file, or replying to an existing comment.

tools.name: Create a review for a pull request
tools.description: Creates a pull request review, allowing approval, change requests, or comments; `body` is required if `event` is `REQUEST_CHANGES` or `COMMENT`, and omitting `event` makes the review `PENDING`.

tools.name: Create a scoped access token
tools.description: Exchanges a user-to-server token for a new, fine-grained scoped access token for a GitHub App, requiring `client_id`, `access_token`, either `target` or `target_id`, and at least one permission; for repository-specific scoping, provide either `repositories` (names) or `repository_ids` (IDs), but not both.

tools.name: Create a dependency snapshot
tools.description: Creates a snapshot of a repository's dependencies to populate the GitHub dependency graph and enable security alerts; `sha` must be a 40-character commit ID, `ref` a fully qualified Git reference (e.g., `refs/heads/main`), and `scanned` an ISO 8601 timestamp.

tools.name: Create a tag object
tools.description: Creates an annotated Git tag object in a repository, pointing to an existing Git object (commit, tree, or blob) defined by its SHA and ensuring the `type` field correctly specifies the object's type.

tools.name: Create a tag protection state for a repository
tools.description: DEPRECATED: This API was sunset on August 30, 2024. Use GITHUB_CREATE_A_REPOSITORY_RULESET instead to create tag protection rules via repository rulesets.

tools.name: Create a team
tools.description: Creates a new team in an organization, optionally with maintainers, repositories, specific privacy, notification settings, or a parent team; if `parent_team_id` is given, `privacy` must be 'closed'.

tools.name: Create a temporary private fork
tools.description: Creates a temporary private fork of the specified repository to address a security vulnerability, linking the fork to a GHSA ID that must be specifically associated with this repository; the fork may take up to 5 minutes to become accessible.

tools.name: Create a tree
tools.description: Creates a new Git tree object in a repository, defining file/directory structure by specifying tree entries, optionally building on a `base_tree` SHA; all provided SHAs must be valid.

tools.name: Create a user project
tools.description: Creates a new GitHub Projects V2 project board for the authenticated user to organize and track issues, pull requests, and notes. Note: This action uses GitHub's Projects V2 GraphQL API. The legacy Projects V1 REST API has been sunset by GitHub.

tools.name: Create a workflow dispatch event
tools.description: Manually triggers a GitHub Actions workflow identified by `workflow_id` at a given `ref`, if the workflow is configured to accept `workflow_dispatch` events.

tools.name: Create commit signature protection
tools.description: Enables commit signature protection for a specified branch, requiring all new commits to be signed.

tools.name: Create a custom deployment protection rule on an environment
tools.description: Enables a custom deployment protection rule for an existing environment in a repository by linking a configured GitHub App (via `integration_id`) to control deployments.

tools.name: Create draft item for user project
tools.description: Creates a draft issue item in a user-owned GitHub ProjectsV2. Use when you need to add a new draft item to track ideas or tasks in a user's project.

tools.name: Create inference chat completions
tools.description: Tool to create chat completions using GitHub Models inference API. Use when you need to generate AI-powered text responses using models like GPT-4, Claude, or Llama through GitHub's inference endpoint.

tools.name: Create inference embeddings
tools.description: Tool to create inference embeddings using GitHub's AI models. Use when you need to convert text into vector representations for similarity search, clustering, or other ML tasks.

tools.name: Create issue type
tools.description: Create a new issue type for a GitHub organization. Requires the authenticated user to be an organization administrator. OAuth tokens need admin:org scope.

tools.name: Create JIT runner config for repo
tools.description: Generates a temporary Just-In-Time (JIT) configuration for a new self-hosted GitHub Actions runner for a repository; any specified non-default `runner_group_id` must be an existing runner group accessible by the repository.

tools.name: Create or update an environment
tools.description: Creates a new environment or updates an existing one in a GitHub repository, allowing configuration of deployment protection rules such as wait timers and reviewers; ensure `environment_name` is URL-encoded if it contains special characters.

tools.name: Create or update an environment secret
tools.description: Creates or updates an environment secret with an `encrypted_value` that was encrypted using the public key identified by `key_id` for the specified environment.

tools.name: Create or update an organization secret
tools.description: Creates or updates an organization secret for GitHub Actions, requiring its value to be pre-encrypted via LibSodium using the organization's public key.

tools.name: Create or update a repository secret
tools.description: Creates or updates a GitHub Actions secret within a specific repository; use `encrypted_value` and `key_id` to set or change its value.

tools.name: Create or update a secret for the authenticated user
tools.description: Creates or updates a Codespaces secret for the authenticated user; `encrypted_value` must be encrypted with the public key (ID: `key_id`) from GitHub's 'Get public key for the authenticated user' endpoint.

tools.name: Create or update custom properties for an organization
tools.description: Creates new custom property schemas or updates existing ones in bulk for a specified organization; each property definition must include `property_name` and `value_type`.

tools.name: Create or update a custom property for an organization
tools.description: Creates a new custom property (name must be unique for creation) or updates an existing one for an organization to define metadata for its repositories.

tools.name: Create or update file contents
tools.description: Creates a new file or updates an existing file in a GitHub repository; SHA can be provided to validate file updates, automatically fetched if not provided.

tools.name: Create or Update GitHub Pages Site
tools.description: Tool to enable or update GitHub Pages configuration for a repository. Use when setting up GitHub Pages for static site deployment or modifying Pages settings like custom domains and HTTPS enforcement.

tools.name: Create or update repo secret with encrypted value
tools.description: Creates or updates a Dependabot secret in a repository using an `encrypted_value` (pre-encrypted with LibSodium using the repository's Dependabot public key) and its corresponding `key_id`. This action allows you to securely manage secrets for a given repository, ensuring that sensitive data remains protected during the update process. By providing the encrypted value alongside the key ID, you can seamlessly maintain the necessary credentials for your repository's operations.

tools.name: Create reaction for a commit comment
tools.description: Creates an emoji reaction for a commit comment; if the user has already reacted with the same content, details of the existing reaction are returned.

tools.name: Create reaction for an issue
tools.description: Creates a reaction for a specified issue within a GitHub repository.

tools.name: Create reaction for an issue comment
tools.description: Creates a reaction for a specific comment on an issue within a GitHub repository.

tools.name: Create reaction for a pull request review comment
tools.description: Adds a specified reaction to a pull request review comment within a GitHub repository.

tools.name: Create reaction for a release
tools.description: Creates an emoji reaction for a specific, existing release in a GitHub repository.

tools.name: Create reaction for a team discussion
tools.description: Creates a reaction for a team discussion within a GitHub organization.

tools.name: Create reaction for a team discussion comment
tools.description: Adds a reaction to a team discussion comment, requiring the specified organization, team, discussion, and comment to exist.

tools.name: Create sponsorship
tools.description: Tool to start a new GitHub sponsorship or reactivate a past sponsorship using GraphQL. Use when you need to sponsor a maintainer through GitHub Sponsors with a specified amount and privacy level.

tools.name: Create Sponsors Tier
tools.description: Tool to create a new payment tier for your GitHub Sponsors profile using GraphQL. Use when you need to add a new sponsorship tier with a specific monthly price and description. The amount is specified in dollars and will be converted to cents automatically.

tools.name: Create or Update Organization Secret with LibSodium
tools.description: Creates or updates a Dependabot organization secret, requiring the secret value to be pre-encrypted with LibSodium using the organization's public key obtained from the 'Get an organization public key' endpoint.

tools.name: Create user list
tools.description: Tool to create a new user list on GitHub. Use when you need to organize and group GitHub users for easier tracking and management.

tools.name: Create view for user project
tools.description: Tool to create a new view in a user-owned GitHub project (Projects V2). Use when you need to add a customized view with specific layout, filters, and visible fields to organize project items. Note: This action works with GitHub Projects V2. The view can be configured with different layouts (table, board, roadmap) and optional filters. The visible_fields parameter is not applicable to roadmap layouts.

tools.name: Decline a repository invitation
tools.description: Declines a specific, pending repository invitation for the authenticated user, identified by its `invitation_id`.

tools.name: Delete access restrictions
tools.description: Removes all user, team, and app-based access restrictions from a protected branch.

tools.name: Delete admin branch protection
tools.description: Removes admin enforcement from a protected branch (branch name cannot contain wildcard characters) in a repository.

tools.name: Delete a file
tools.description: Deletes a file by path from a GitHub repository. The file's blob SHA is automatically fetched if not provided.

tools.name: Delete a package version for the authenticated user
tools.description: Deletes an existing package version associated with the authenticated user.

tools.name: Delete an app authorization
tools.description: Deletes an OAuth application grant for a user, which revokes ALL OAuth tokens and their associated authorizations for the application. This endpoint is only accessible to OAuth App owners and requires Basic Authentication using the OAuth App's client_id and client_secret.

tools.name: Delete an app token
tools.description: Revokes a single OAuth access token for an OAuth App or GitHub App with OAuth authorization. IMPORTANT: This endpoint requires Basic Authentication using the OAuth App's client_id as username and client_secret as password. It CANNOT be called with personal access tokens, GitHub App installation tokens, or any other token type. You must be the OAuth App owner to use this endpoint.

tools.name: Delete a reference
tools.description: Deletes a Git reference from a repository; 'ref' must be fully qualified (e.g., 'refs/heads/branch' or 'refs/tags/tag').

tools.name: Delete a release
tools.description: Permanently deletes a specific release, its assets, and potentially its associated Git tag from a repository.

tools.name: Delete a release asset
tools.description: Deletes a specific release asset from a GitHub repository; this action is idempotent.

tools.name: Delete a release reaction
tools.description: Deletes a reaction from a GitHub release, provided the repository, release, and reaction exist.

tools.name: Delete a repository
tools.description: Permanently deletes the specified repository; this is a destructive, irreversible action that requires admin privileges for the repository.

tools.name: Delete a repository invitation
tools.description: Deletes an active repository invitation, permanently revoking a user's access to collaborate on the specified repository.

tools.name: Delete a repository ruleset
tools.description: Permanently deletes a repository ruleset.

tools.name: Delete a repository secret
tools.description: Deletes a named GitHub Actions secret from a specified repository; this operation is destructive and idempotent, and requires the repository to exist.

tools.name: Delete a repository subscription
tools.description: Deletes the authenticated user's subscription to a specified repository if it exists, effectively 'unwatching' it.

tools.name: Delete a repository variable
tools.description: Deletes a named variable (e.g., for GitHub Actions workflows) from a repository; the repository and the variable must already exist.

tools.name: Delete a repository webhook
tools.description: Deletes a specific webhook from a repository.

tools.name: Delete a review comment for a pull request
tools.description: Deletes a specific pull request review comment.

tools.name: Delete an artifact
tools.description: Deletes a GitHub artifact by its ID within a repository, typically resulting in an empty response (HTTP 204 No Content) on success.

tools.name: Delete a secret for the authenticated user
tools.description: Deletes an existing Codespaces secret for the authenticated user by `secret_name`. This is a destructive and irreversible operation. Returns 404 if the secret does not exist.

tools.name: Delete a self hosted runner from an organization
tools.description: Forces the removal of a self-hosted runner from a GitHub organization. This endpoint can be used to completely remove the runner when the machine you were using no longer exists. The runner will be immediately disconnected from GitHub Actions. Requires admin:org scope and organization admin access. Returns 204 No Content on successful deletion.

tools.name: Delete a self hosted runner from a repository
tools.description: Removes a specific self-hosted runner (by `runner_id`) from a repository, if registered there; this is idempotent.

tools.name: Delete a tag protection state for a repository
tools.description: DEPRECATED: This API was sunset on August 30, 2024. Use GITHUB_DELETE_A_REPOSITORY_RULESET instead to manage tag protection rules via repository rulesets.

tools.name: Delete a team
tools.description: Deletes a team (and any child teams) from an organization.

tools.name: Delete a thread subscription
tools.description: Call this to mute a specific notification thread by deleting the user's subscription; notifications may still occur if the user is @mentioned, comments, or due to repository watch settings.

tools.name: Delete an autolink reference from a repository
tools.description: Deletes a specific autolink reference (which automatically links external resource IDs like JIRA-123 to URLs) from the specified repository.

tools.name: Delete a workflow run
tools.description: Deletes a specific workflow run from a repository.

tools.name: Delete branch protection
tools.description: Removes all protection rules from a specific branch in a GitHub repository; the branch must currently have protection rules enabled.

tools.name: Delete a code scanning analysis from a repository
tools.description: Deletes a specific code scanning analysis by its ID from a repository; `confirm_delete` must be `true` if it's the last analysis of its type for a given tool and reference to prevent data loss.

tools.name: Delete a codespace for the authenticated user
tools.description: Deletes a specific codespace owned by the authenticated user; this is a destructive action and the codespace must exist.

tools.name: Delete a commit comment
tools.description: Deletes a specific commit comment, identified by its `comment_id`, from the specified repository; the comment must exist.

tools.name: Delete a commit comment reaction
tools.description: Deletes a reaction from a commit comment in a GitHub repository.

tools.name: Delete commit signature protection
tools.description: Disables GPG commit signature protection for a specific branch in a GitHub repository, meaning commits pushed to this branch no longer require GPG signing.

tools.name: Delete a custom organization role
tools.description: Deletes a custom organization role (which should not be actively assigned) by its ID; a 204 No Content response indicates success.

tools.name: Delete dependabot secret by name
tools.description: Deletes a specific Dependabot secret, identified by its name, from a given repository if both the repository and secret exist.

tools.name: Delete a deploy key
tools.description: Deletes a specific deploy key from a repository; to change a key's properties or access scope, the existing key must be deleted and a new one created.

tools.name: Delete a deployment
tools.description: Permanently deletes a specified *inactive* deployment from a repository.

tools.name: Delete a deployment branch policy
tools.description: Deletes a specific deployment branch or tag policy, identified by its ID, from a given environment within a repository.

tools.name: Delete a discussion
tools.description: Deletes a specific team discussion, identified by its number, from an organization's team.

tools.name: Delete a discussion comment
tools.description: Deletes a specific comment from an existing team discussion within an organization, provided the specified organization, team, discussion, and comment all exist.

tools.name: Delete authenticated user email address
tools.description: Sends an empty request body to `DELETE /user/emails` to attempt deletion of user email addresses; the API typically requires specific emails, so outcome may vary.

tools.name: Delete an environment
tools.description: Deletes an existing deployment environment from an existing repository.

tools.name: Delete an environment secret
tools.description: Deletes an existing and accessible secret from a specified environment within a GitHub repository, returning an empty dictionary on success or error details otherwise.

tools.name: Delete an environment variable
tools.description: Deletes a named environment variable from a specified, existing environment within a GitHub repository.

tools.name: Delete a gist
tools.description: Permanently deletes an existing GitHub gist, specified by its `gist_id`; this action is destructive and cannot be undone.

tools.name: Delete a gist comment
tools.description: Deletes a specific comment from a GitHub Gist using its `gist_id` and `comment_id`.

tools.name: Delete GitHub Actions cache by ID
tools.description: Deletes a specific GitHub Actions cache from a repository using its unique `cache_id`.

tools.name: Delete a GitHub Pages site
tools.description: Deletes the GitHub Pages site for the specified repository; completes without error if no site is currently enabled.

tools.name: Delete an issue comment
tools.description: Permanently deletes a specific comment by its ID from an issue or pull request, if the repository exists and the comment ID is valid.

tools.name: Delete an issue comment reaction
tools.description: Deletes a reaction from an issue comment in a repository; the repository, comment, and reaction must exist.

tools.name: Delete an issue reaction
tools.description: Permanently removes a specific reaction from an issue in a GitHub repository.

tools.name: Delete a label
tools.description: Permanently removes an existing label from a repository.

tools.name: Delete a milestone
tools.description: Deletes the specified milestone if it exists; this operation is idempotent, typically returning a 404 if the milestone is not found or already deleted.

tools.name: Delete an organization
tools.description: Deletes a GitHub organization and its repositories; this is a destructive action and the organization name will be unavailable for reuse for approximately 90 days.

tools.name: Delete an organization secret
tools.description: Permanently deletes a secret from a GitHub organization, making it inaccessible to GitHub Actions workflows or other tools.

tools.name: Delete an organization variable
tools.description: Deletes a named GitHub Actions variable from a specified organization.

tools.name: Delete an organization webhook
tools.description: Deletes a specific webhook, identified by `hook_id`, from an existing organization.

tools.name: Delete a codespace from the organization
tools.description: Permanently deletes a specific codespace belonging to a member of the specified organization.

tools.name: Delete a package for an organization
tools.description: Deletes a specific package in an organization; cannot delete public packages with over 5,000 downloads.

tools.name: Delete a package for the authenticated user
tools.description: Permanently deletes a specific package owned by the authenticated user; public packages downloaded over 5,000 times cannot be deleted via this API.

tools.name: Delete package version
tools.description: Tool to delete a package version using GitHub GraphQL API. Use when you need to remove a specific version of a package by its global node ID.

tools.name: Delete package version for an organization
tools.description: Deletes a specific package version within an organization; requires admin permissions for packages with over 5,000 downloads.

tools.name: Delete package version for a user
tools.description: Permanently and irreversibly deletes a specific version of a package owned by the specified user.

tools.name: Delete a pending review for a pull request
tools.description: Deletes a pending (unsubmitted) review from a pull request; this is only possible if the review has not yet been submitted.

tools.name: Delete a project
tools.description: Deletes the specified GitHub project (Projects V2) using the GraphQL API. Note: This action uses GitHub's Projects V2 GraphQL API. The legacy Projects (classic) REST API was sunset on April 1, 2025 and is no longer available. The project is permanently deleted and cannot be recovered. The user must have admin permissions for the project to delete it.

tools.name: Delete a project card (Classic - Deprecated)
tools.description: Deletes a project card from a GitHub 'Project (classic)'; this operation is idempotent. DEPRECATION NOTICE: GitHub Classic Projects (V1) and its REST API were sunset on April 1, 2025. This action may return a 404 error on GitHub.com. For new projects, use GitHub Projects V2 which uses the GraphQL API instead. See: https://github.blog/changelog/2024-05-23-sunset-notice-projects-classic/

tools.name: Delete a project field (column)
tools.description: Deletes a project field (column) from a GitHub Projects V2 project using the GraphQL API. IMPORTANT: GitHub Classic Projects REST API was sunset on April 1, 2025. This action now uses the GitHub Projects V2 GraphQL API with the deleteProjectV2Field mutation. Note: The built-in Status field cannot be deleted as it is a core field in GitHub Projects V2. Only custom fields can be deleted.

tools.name: Delete project item for user
tools.description: Tool to delete a project item for a user in GitHub Projects V2. Use when you need to remove an item from a user's project. Requires the project item's GraphQL node ID (starts with 'PVTI_'). Uses the GitHub GraphQL API deleteProjectV2Item mutation.

tools.name: Delete a pull request comment reaction
tools.description: Deletes a specific reaction from a pull request review comment, provided the comment and reaction exist on that comment within the specified repository.

tools.name: Delete pull request review protection
tools.description: Disables the requirement for pull request reviews before merging for a specific, existing branch in an existing repository; this action is idempotent and will succeed even if the protection is not currently enabled.

tools.name: Delete repo codespace secret by name
tools.description: Deletes a specific Codespace secret from a repository by its name; this action is idempotent and will succeed even if the secret doesn't exist.

tools.name: Delete social accounts for the authenticated user
tools.description: Deletes currently linked social media account URLs from the authenticated user's GitHub profile.

tools.name: Delete team discussion comment reaction
tools.description: Deletes a reaction from a team discussion comment, given the organization name, team slug, discussion number, comment number, and reaction ID.

tools.name: Delete team discussion reaction
tools.description: Permanently deletes a specific reaction from a team discussion within an organization.

tools.name: Delete User List
tools.description: Tool to delete a GitHub user list using GraphQL. Use when you need to remove a user list from a GitHub account.

tools.name: Delete a package for a user
tools.description: Deletes a package owned by the specified user, requiring admin permissions for the authenticated user; deletion of public packages with over 5,000 downloads may require GitHub support.

tools.name: Delete workflow run logs
tools.description: Deletes all logs for a specific workflow run in a GitHub repository, provided the repository and run exist.

tools.name: Disable a custom protection rule for an environment
tools.description: Disables a specific, currently active custom deployment protection rule for an existing environment within a GitHub repository.

tools.name: Disable a workflow
tools.description: Disables a specified workflow (by ID or filename) in a given GitHub repository, preventing new automatic triggers; any in-progress runs will continue.

tools.name: Disable private vulnerability reporting for a repository
tools.description: Disables private vulnerability reporting for an existing GitHub repository, preventing direct private vulnerability reports to maintainers via GitHub's interface for this repository.

tools.name: Disable Repository Actions In Org
tools.description: Removes a repository from the list of selected repositories enabled for GitHub Actions in an organization. Only works when the organization's `enabled_repositories` policy is set to `selected`. Requires admin:org scope.

tools.name: Dismiss a review for a pull request
tools.description: Dismisses an APPROVED or CHANGES_REQUESTED review on a pull request with a mandatory explanatory message. IMPORTANT: Only reviews in APPROVED or CHANGES_REQUESTED state can be dismissed. Reviews in COMMENTED, PENDING, or already DISMISSED state will return a 422 error. To dismiss a review on a protected branch, you must be a repository admin or be authorized to dismiss pull request reviews.

tools.name: Download an artifact
tools.description: Downloads a GitHub Actions workflow artifact as a ZIP file. Returns the artifact as a downloadable file. Use GITHUB_LIST_ARTIFACTS_FOR_A_REPOSITORY or GITHUB_LIST_WORKFLOW_RUN_ARTIFACTS to get valid artifact IDs first.

tools.name: Download a repository tarball
tools.description: Downloads a repository's source code as a tarball (.tar.gz) archive for a specific Git reference, if the repository is accessible.

tools.name: Download a repository archive ZIP
tools.description: Downloads a repository's source code as a ZIP archive for a specific Git reference (branch, tag, or commit SHA). IMPORTANT SIZE LIMITATION: This action may fail with 'payload too large' errors for large repositories due to platform size restrictions. If you encounter size limit issues, consider these alternatives: - Use GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT to fetch specific files or directories (also lists directory contents) - Clone the repository using git if you need the full codebase Best suited for: small to medium repositories, downloading specific tagged releases, or quick code inspection.

tools.name: Download job logs for a workflow run
tools.description: Downloads logs for a specific job in a GitHub Actions workflow run, contingent on the repository's existence and the job ID being valid and having produced logs.

tools.name: Download workflow run attempt logs
tools.description: Downloads a ZIP archive of logs for a specific workflow run attempt. Returns a downloadable ZIP file containing logs for all jobs and steps in the workflow run.

tools.name: Download workflow run logs
tools.description: Downloads logs for a specific GitHub Actions workflow run as a ZIP archive containing log files for each job in the workflow.

tools.name: Enable a workflow
tools.description: Reactivates a currently disabled GitHub Actions workflow within a repository using its workflow ID or filename.

tools.name: Enable GitHub actions in selected repositories
tools.description: Sets the specific repositories that can use GitHub Actions within an organization by replacing the current list; only applies if the organization's Actions policy is 'selected repositories'.

tools.name: Enable private vulnerability reporting for a repository
tools.description: Enables private vulnerability reporting for a repository, allowing security researchers to privately submit vulnerability reports to maintainers.

tools.name: Enable repo for Github Actions
tools.description: Adds a repository to the list of selected repositories enabled for GitHub Actions in an organization. Requires the organization's 'enabled_repositories' policy to be set to 'selected'.

tools.name: Encrypt and update dev secret
tools.description: Creates or updates a repository's development environment secret using an `encrypted_value` and its corresponding `key_id`; the secret must be pre-encrypted with the repository's Codespaces public key.

tools.name: Encrypt org dev env secret
tools.description: Creates or updates an organization's GitHub Codespaces secret using an encrypted value and its corresponding public key ID.

tools.name: Export a codespace for the authenticated user
tools.description: Triggers an export of a user's specified codespace, automatically stopping it if active, and returns its export status and download URL.

tools.name: Export an SBOM for a repository
tools.description: Exports the software bill of materials (SBOM) in SPDX JSON format for a repository, if its dependency graph is enabled and it has at least one commit.

tools.name: Find Pull Requests
tools.description: Primary tool to find and search pull requests. Supports filtering by repository, author, state, labels, and merge status, and returns structured PR data for reliable use in workflows. GitHub search results are capped at ~1000 total items; narrow filters when totals approach this limit. `created_since`/`updated_since` filter on creation/update timestamps, not `merged_at`; apply merge-date filtering client-side.

tools.name: Find Repositories
tools.description: AI-optimized repository search with smart filtering by language, stars, topics, and ownership. Builds intelligent search queries and returns clean, actionable repository data. Check `incomplete_results` in the response — when true, results are non-exhaustive. Search endpoints are rate-limited to ~30 requests/minute (vs. 5000/hour for general REST); apply backoff on 403/429. Total results are capped at ~1000 per query regardless of pagination.

tools.name: Follow Organization (GraphQL)
tools.description: Tool to follow a GitHub organization using GraphQL. Use when you need to make the authenticated user follow an organization.

tools.name: Follow a user
tools.description: Allows the authenticated user to follow the GitHub user specified by `username`; this action is idempotent and the user cannot follow themselves.

tools.name: Follow User (GraphQL)
tools.description: Tool to follow a GitHub user using GraphQL. Use when you need to make the authenticated user follow another user.

tools.name: Force cancel a workflow run
tools.description: Forcefully cancels a queued or in-progress GitHub Actions workflow run, bypassing conditions like always() that would otherwise continue execution. Only use when the standard cancel endpoint fails. Cannot cancel completed workflow runs. Requires write permissions to the repository.

tools.name: Fork a gist
tools.description: Forks a specified public gist, creating a copy under the authenticated user's account.

tools.name: Generate release notes content for a release
tools.description: Generates Markdown release notes content (listing changes, pull requests, and contributors) for a GitHub repository release, customizable via tags and a configuration file.

tools.name: Get a blob
tools.description: Retrieves the raw, typically Base64-encoded, content of a file (blob) from a GitHub repository using its SHA hash, if the repository and blob SHA exist.

tools.name: Get a branch
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information for a specified branch within a GitHub repository.

tools.name: Get access restrictions
tools.description: Lists users, teams, and GitHub Apps with push access to a branch; this branch must be protected in repository settings for detailed restrictions, otherwise expect a 404 or empty response.

tools.name: Get a commit
tools.description: Retrieves a specific commit from a repository by its owner, name, and a valid commit reference (SHA, branch, or tag), supporting pagination for large diffs.

tools.name: Get admin branch protection
tools.description: Checks if repository administrators are subject to the branch protection rules on a specific branch.

tools.name: Get all API versions
tools.description: Retrieves all officially supported, date-based (e.g., "2022-11-28") versions of the GitHub REST API from the /versions endpoint.

tools.name: Get all contributor commit activity
tools.description: Retrieves commit activity (total commits, weekly additions/deletions/commits) for all contributors to a repository; may require a retry if GitHub returns 202 while preparing data.

tools.name: Get all deployment protection rules for an environment
tools.description: Lists all enabled custom deployment protection rules for a specific environment in a repository; the environment must exist and be configured for deployments.

tools.name: Get a milestone
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information for a specific milestone within a GitHub repository by its number.

tools.name: Get an app
tools.description: Retrieves publicly available information for an existing GitHub App, identified by its unique URL-friendly `app_slug`.

tools.name: Get an artifact
tools.description: Gets a specific artifact for a repository by `artifact_id`. This action retrieves the details of a specific artifact from a GitHub repository using the artifact's unique identifier. It allows users to access information about artifacts stored in the repository.

tools.name: Get an assignment
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information for a specific GitHub Classroom assignment if the authenticated user is an administrator of the classroom.

tools.name: Get an autolink reference of a repository
tools.description: Retrieves a specific autolink reference (which automatically hyperlinks text like 'JIRA-123' to an external system) for a repository using its unique ID; requires administrator access to the repository.

tools.name: Get an environment
tools.description: Retrieves the details of a specific deployment environment for a given repository, including its name, configurations, and current status.

tools.name: Get an environment public key
tools.description: Retrieves the public key for a specified GitHub repository environment, used to encrypt secrets for GitHub Actions.

tools.name: Get an environment secret
tools.description: Retrieves metadata (name and timestamps) for a single secret in a GitHub Actions environment. Note: The actual secret value is never returned by this API for security reasons.

tools.name: Get an environment variable
tools.description: Retrieves a specific environment variable from a GitHub Actions environment by repository owner, repository name, environment name, and variable name.

tools.name: Get an issue
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific issue in a repository using the owner, repository name, and issue number.

tools.name: Get an issue comment
tools.description: Action to get an issue comment.

tools.name: Get an issue event
tools.description: Fetches details of a specific issue event for a given repository and event ID.

tools.name: Get an organization
tools.description: Get an organization

tools.name: Get an organization public key
tools.description: Action for `GetAnOrganizationPublicKey`.

tools.name: Get an organization role
tools.description: Retrieves a specific GitHub organization role by its ID.

tools.name: Get an organization secret
tools.description: Gets an organization secret's metadata (e.g., name, creation/update dates, visibility), but not its encrypted value.

tools.name: Get an organization variable
tools.description: Retrieves details (name, value, visibility, timestamps) of a specific, existing variable for an existing GitHub organization.

tools.name: Get an organization webhook
tools.description: Retrieves the full configuration, including subscribed events and delivery settings, for an existing organization webhook.

tools.name: Get a package for an organization
tools.description: Retrieves a specific package (by type and name) from an organization, if both the package and organization exist.

tools.name: Get a package for a user
tools.description: Retrieves metadata for a specific package owned by a GitHub user, using package type, name, and username as identifiers.

tools.name: Get a package for the authenticated user
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information for a specific package owned by the authenticated user.

tools.name: Get a package version for an organization
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information for a specific version of a package within an organization.

tools.name: Get a package version for a user
tools.description: Retrieves a specific public package version associated with a GitHub user.

tools.name: Get authenticated user package version
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information for an existing specific package version associated with the authenticated user, identified by its type, name, and version ID.

tools.name: Get a project
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information for a specific GitHub project (V2) using its project number and owner. Note: This action uses GitHub's Projects V2 REST API. The legacy Projects (classic) REST API was sunset on April 1, 2025. The project is identified by its number (visible in the project URL) and owner (either a username or organization name). If no owner is specified, the authenticated user is assumed.

tools.name: Get a project card
tools.description: Retrieves all details of a specific project card, given its unique `card_id`. DEPRECATION NOTICE: GitHub Projects (classic) REST API was sunset on April 1, 2025. This action only works with existing classic project cards that were created before the sunset date. For new projects, use GitHub Projects V2 (GraphQL API) instead.

tools.name: Get a project column (Classic - Deprecated)
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information for a specific project column from GitHub Projects (classic). DEPRECATION NOTICE: GitHub Classic Projects (V1) and its REST API were sunset on April 1, 2025. This action will return 404 for most requests on GitHub.com. However, it may still work on GitHub Enterprise Server instances where classic projects are enabled. For new projects, use GitHub Projects V2 which uses the GraphQL API instead. See: https://github.blog/changelog/2024-05-23-sunset-notice-projects-classic/ Returns column details including: id, name, url, project_url, cards_url, node_id, created_at, and updated_at timestamps.

tools.name: Get a pull request
tools.description: Retrieves a specific pull request from a GitHub repository using its owner, repository name, and pull request number.

tools.name: Get a reference
tools.description: Retrieves a specific Git reference (e.g., a branch, tag, or fully qualified like 'heads/main') from a GitHub repository. The reference must exist in the repository; use 'list_matching_references' first if unsure what references are available.

tools.name: Get a release
tools.description: Gets a specific release from a GitHub repository, provided the repository is accessible and the release exists.

tools.name: Get a release asset
tools.description: Gets metadata for a specific release asset in a GitHub repository, including a `browser_download_url` for downloading the asset.

tools.name: Get a release by tag name
tools.description: Gets a release from a GitHub repository by its tag name; the repository and a release with this tag must already exist.

tools.name: Get a repository
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information about an existing and accessible GitHub repository.

tools.name: Get a repository public key
tools.description: Gets a repository's public key for encrypting secrets to be used in GitHub Actions, if the repository exists and is accessible.

tools.name: Get a repository readme
tools.description: Fetches the README file (if it exists and is accessible) from a specified GitHub repository, returning its Base64-encoded content and metadata.

tools.name: Get a repository readme for a directory
tools.description: Retrieves the README file from a specified directory within a GitHub repository, optionally at a given commit, branch, or tag.

tools.name: Get a repository ruleset
tools.description: Retrieves a specific repository ruleset by its ID; if `includes_parents` is true, the search for this `ruleset_id` also extends to rulesets from parent organizations.

tools.name: Get a repository rule suite
tools.description: Gets detailed information for a specific repository rule suite by its ID, including its evaluation status and the results of its individual rules.

tools.name: Get a repository secret
tools.description: Gets metadata (name, creation/update timestamps) for an existing repository secret, excluding its encrypted value.

tools.name: Get a repository subscription
tools.description: Gets the authenticated user's subscription details for a repository, indicating if they receive notifications.

tools.name: Get a repository variable
tools.description: Gets a specific GitHub Actions variable by name from an accessible repository.

tools.name: Get a repository webhook
tools.description: Returns the configuration of an existing webhook for a given repository.

tools.name: Get a review comment for a pull request
tools.description: Retrieves a specific pull request review comment by its ID, provided the repository exists, is accessible, and the comment ID is valid.

tools.name: Get a review for a pull request
tools.description: Retrieves a specific review for a pull request using its owner, repository, pull request number, and review ID.

tools.name: Get a secret for the authenticated user
tools.description: Retrieves metadata (name, timestamps, visibility; not the value) for a specific, existing development environment secret associated with the authenticated user's GitHub Codespaces.

tools.name: Get a self hosted runner for an organization
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific self-hosted runner registered within a GitHub organization.

tools.name: Get a self hosted runner for a repository
tools.description: Gets a specific self-hosted runner for a repository by its unique ID.

tools.name: Get assignment grades
tools.description: Retrieves all grades for an existing GitHub Classroom assignment.

tools.name: Get a tag
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information for a specific Git tag object from a GitHub repository, using the SHA of the tag object itself.

tools.name: Get a team by name
tools.description: Retrieves a GitHub team by its slug from a specific organization.

tools.name: Get a thread
tools.description: Retrieves a specific GitHub notification thread using its unique `thread_id`.

tools.name: Get a thread subscription for the authenticated user
tools.description: Retrieves the authenticated user's subscription details for a specific notification thread, identified by `thread_id`.

tools.name: List repository files and directories
tools.description: Browse and list all files/directories in a GitHub repository. Efficiently retrieves the complete repository structure in a single API call when used with recursive mode. Perfect for analyzing codebase structure, finding specific files, or getting an overview of repository contents without cloning.

tools.name: Get a user
tools.description: Retrieves the public profile information for an existing GitHub user, specified by their username.

tools.name: Get a webhook configuration for an organization
tools.description: Retrieves the configuration for a specific webhook associated with a GitHub organization.

tools.name: Get a webhook configuration for a repository
tools.description: Returns the configuration for an existing webhook on the specified repository.

tools.name: Get a webhook delivery for an organization webhook
tools.description: Returns detailed information for a specific delivery attempt of a webhook configured for the specified GitHub organization.

tools.name: Get a workflow

tools.name: Get a check suite

tools.name: Get a code of conduct

tools.name: Get Code of Conduct (GraphQL)

tools.name: Get a CodeQL database for a repository

tools.name: Get a code scanning alert

tools.name: Get a code scanning analysis for a repository

tools.name: Get a code scanning default setup configuration

tools.name: Get a codespace for the authenticated user

tools.name: Get commit authors

tools.name: Get a commit comment

tools.name: Get a commit object

tools.name: Get commit signature protection

tools.name: Get commit statuses
tools.description: List all statuses for a commit reference (SHA, branch, or tag) in reverse chronological order. Use when you need to check CI/CD status results from various systems for a specific commit.

tools.name: Get community profile metrics

tools.name: Get contextual information for a user

tools.name: Get a custom deployment protection rule

tools.name: Get default attributes for a codespace

tools.name: Get default workflow permissions for an organization

tools.name: Get a diff of the dependencies between commits

tools.name: Get a deploy key

tools.name: Get a deployment

tools.name: Get a deployment branch policy

tools.name: Get a deployment status

tools.name: Get details about a codespace export
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific export of a codespace.

tools.name: Get a discussion

tools.name: Get a discussion comment
tools.description: Fetches a specific comment from a team discussion within a specific organization.

tools.name: Get emojis
tools.description: Lists all emojis available for use on GitHub, including custom and Unicode emojis.

tools.name: Get Enterprise Member Invitation
tools.description: Tool to look up a pending enterprise unaffiliated member invitation by invitee and enterprise. Use when you need to check the status of a specific invitation.

tools.name: Get feeds
tools.description: Fetches a list of available GitHub feed URLs for the authenticated user.

tools.name: Get a gist
tools.description: Fetches a specific GitHub gist by its `gist_id`, returning comprehensive details if the gist exists.

tools.name: Get a gist comment
tools.description: Retrieves a specific Gist comment by its ID and the Gist's ID.

tools.name: Get a gist revision
tools.description: Retrieves a specific revision of a gist.

tools.name: Get GitHub Actions cache usage for an organization
tools.description: Retrieves total GitHub Actions cache usage statistics for an organization, including active cache count and size across all repositories.

tools.name: Get github actions cache usage for a repository

tools.name: Get github actions permissions for an organization
tools.description: Gets the GitHub Actions permissions for a specified organization, detailing repository enablement and allowed actions policies.

tools.name: Get GitHub Actions permissions for a repository
tools.description: Gets the GitHub Actions permissions policy for a repository, including its enabled status and the scope of allowed actions.

tools.name: Get billing premium request usage
tools.description: Tool to get billing premium request usage report for a GitHub user. Use when you need to retrieve usage data for premium features like Copilot or AI models.

tools.name: Get billing usage summary for user
tools.description: Tool to retrieve billing usage summary for a GitHub user account. Use when tracking usage costs, monitoring billing details, or generating usage reports for a specific user. Note: This endpoint only returns data for the past 24 months and is currently in public preview.

tools.name: Get github meta information
tools.description: Fetches GitHub's publicly available metadata, useful for configuring network security policies or IP allow-listing.

tools.name: Get github pages build
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific GitHub Pages build for a repository, which must have GitHub Pages enabled.

tools.name: Get a gitignore template
tools.description: Retrieves a specific .gitignore template from GitHub by its name, which must be an existing template in GitHub's collection.

tools.name: Get a global security advisory

tools.name: Fetch GraphQL Node
tools.description: Tool to fetch any GitHub object by its global node ID. Use when you have a node_id and need to retrieve the corresponding object details.

tools.name: Get GraphQL rate limit

tools.name: Get information about a sarif upload

tools.name: Get interaction restrictions for an organization

tools.name: Get interaction restrictions for a repository
tools.description: Retrieves active interaction restrictions for a repository, detailing which user groups are limited from activities like commenting or creating pull requests, and when these restrictions expire.

tools.name: Get interaction restrictions for public repositories
tools.description: Retrieves currently active interaction restrictions for the authenticated user's public repositories.

tools.name: Get a label
tools.description: Retrieves a specific label by its name from a specified GitHub repository.

tools.name: Get large files
tools.description: Lists files larger than 100MB identified during a previous source import for the specified repository. Please use the GitHub Importer tool at https://github.com/new/import for repository imports.

tools.name: Get latest pages build
tools.description: Retrieves information about the most recent GitHub Pages build for a repository, which must exist, be accessible, have GitHub Pages enabled, and have at least one prior build.

tools.name: Get a license

tools.name: Get License (GraphQL)
tools.description: Tool to look up an open source license by its SPDX ID using GitHub's GraphQL API. Use when you need to fetch license details for compliance tracking or repository setup.

tools.name: Get octocat

tools.name: Customize OIDC subject claim template
tools.description: Retrieves the OpenID Connect (OIDC) subject claim customization template for a repository, which defines the `sub` claim structure in OIDC tokens for GitHub Actions workflows; returns the default configuration if no customization is applied.

tools.name: Get allowed actions and workflows for an org
tools.description: Gets the list of allowed actions and reusable workflows for an organization when the 'allowed_actions' policy is set to 'selected'.

tools.name: Get organization audit log
tools.description: Tool to retrieve an organization's audit log events for security and compliance investigations. Use when tracking organizational changes, security audits, or compliance monitoring. Requires organization owner permissions and read:audit_log scope.

tools.name: Get a custom property for an organization
tools.description: Retrieves the definition (schema) of a specific, existing custom property for an organization.

tools.name: Get organization project item
tools.description: Tool to get an item from an organization-owned GitHub Projects V2 project. Use when you need to retrieve details about a specific project item including its content, fields, timestamps, and creator information.

tools.name: Get organization public key for Codespaces secrets
tools.description: Retrieves an organization's public key, which must be used to encrypt secret values before they are configured for Codespaces.

tools.name: Fetch Public Key For Secret Encryption
tools.description: Retrieves the public key for an existing GitHub organization, required for encrypting Dependabot secrets. Requires admin:org scope.

tools.name: Get org dev environment secret safely
tools.description: Retrieves metadata for a specific secret available to an organization's GitHub Codespaces without exposing its encrypted value.

tools.name: Get custom OIDC subject claim template
tools.description: Retrieves the OpenID Connect (OIDC) subject claim customization template for a GitHub organization, which defines how the `sub` claim in OIDC tokens for workflows is constructed.

tools.name: Get a dns health check for github pages
tools.description: Retrieves the DNS health check status (e.g., CNAME/A records, HTTPS) for a GitHub Pages site; the check may be pending (HTTP 202) on initial calls or after site changes.

tools.name: Get pull request review protection

tools.name: Get allowed actions and workflows for a repository
